relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Inherited values, replacement metacharacters and Symbol conversion cause real defects.

defects: Senior used replaceAll despite the requested replace exercise and interpolated Symbols instead of calling String.
Whitespace grammar, primitive domain, nonrecursive insertion and copying costs were implicit.
All old tests accepted a Symbol-throwing implementation.
rationale: Use replace and String in senior, preserving the correct reference/junior. Define ASCII word names, JavaScript whitespace, literal/nonrecursive replacement, unchanged read-only data records and bounded primitive values including Symbol/BigInt/null/undefined. State a conservative quadratic backtracking/copying upper bound with input/output size, without claiming an engine guarantee. Add null-prototype/frozen records, Symbol conversion, tabs/newlines, invalid names, literal dollar/braces, unchanged missing whitespace and a 3000-blank expansion.

objective: Replace pending trailing-edge deliveries while preserving exact argument identity and allowing later/reentrant bursts.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: Debouncing remains a standard event-handling technique.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Delayed saving and search input need the latest pending arguments.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Closure ownership, cancellation and opaque value forwarding transfer widely.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: Bounded callbacks/arguments and minimum waits avoid timer precision claims.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Cloning values or running zero-delay callbacks inline breaks real integrations.

defects: Zero delay, opaque argument identity, wrapper returns and callback-started bursts were implicit.
The cost scope omitted rest/spread and host waiting.
Cloning argument lists passed all prior primitive-only cases.
rationale: Retain all correct supplied boards. Bound calls/arguments and define O(n) rest/spread work per call/delivery excluding host timers, waiting and fn. Add 10000 immediate replacements with a zero-delay final opaque object/Symbol/undefined/signed-zero list and a callback-started second burst.

objective: Gate leading-edge calls by one Date.now timestamp, including exact boundaries and consumed error/reentry windows.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: Leading-edge throttling remains a practical event-handling technique.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Rate-limiting a synchronous callback requires a clear eligibility window.
relevanceRationale.transferable: State-before-callback and exact boundary comparisons generalize to guards.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: A bounded nondecreasing clock and argument model keep scope explicit.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Reset-timer queue order and callback errors can leave a wrapper blocked.

defects: Before b040, junior installed its reset timer after fn, so a thrown callback permanently blocked later calls; reference read Date.now twice.

B040 revision 1 over-constrained clock access and its Date.now-only stubs rejected the existing valid new Date().getTime() integrity implementation. Captured clock aliases also require the unchanged coherent runtime clock.
rationale: Retain the corrected timestamp-based reference/junior/senior and the intended consumed-error/reentry window. Accept equivalent Date timestamp reads and aliases; do not replace a clock global inside functional grading. Replace fake-time exact-boundary cases with normal-clock opaque argument/undefined-return checks, consumed original-error and reentry checks followed by a comfortably later timer, and a 10000-call burst that asserts valid accepted ordering without inventing an exact count. Exact >= boundary and drop non-extension are established by reading the supplied implementations, not a wall-clock benchmark. Add valid captured Date-constructor and Date.now-alias candidates. The pre-existing whole grading-integrity suite caught the bad revision before this cohort was merged or deployed; its new Date proof is preserved and a captured Date.now proof is now permanent. No runtime-engine or reward-policy change.
